## First LIVE occurrence outside a contention test — ops error sweep 2026-08-11/12

This ticket's mechanism (a write whose lock acquire times out is permanently lost) was observed **in a live external-integration run against real Jira DC**, not in a synthetic contention harness.

**Run:** GitHub Actions 'Live External Integration', 2026-08-10T06:31Z, run 31427-series (single failure in the sweep window 2026-08-05 -> 2026-08-12T03:30Z).

**Verbatim:**

    rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s
    AssertionError: second pass: the repeated pass did NOT report convergence - it wrote something
    tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:184

**Why this is evidence for THIS ticket and not merely a slow-CI flake:** the two lines are causally linked in exactly the way this ticket predicts. The 30s lock-acquire timeout made pass 1's write disappear with no durable record; pass 2 therefore found the work undone and wrote it again, which broke the reconciler's **idempotency/convergence invariant**. The lost write is not just lost data here — it is observable as a correctness failure in a different subsystem, which is the strongest available argument that the terminal-and-lossy budget is not an acceptable steady state.

This also means the blast radius is wider than local high-concurrency use: a single ordinary CI runner under normal load can spend the 30s budget.

Related sighting the same week: tests/interfaces/store/test_git_contention_9305.py::test_concurrent_processes_through_seam_both_succeed failed 2026-08-11T13:05Z with 'writer beta failed' (assert 1 == 0 on the subprocess return code) - the same lock-contention family, from the regression test of bug 9305.

Reported by an automated ops error sweep; no code changed.
